title: Ackee and Saltfish
subtitle: jamaica's national dish with salt cod
excerpt: Ackee and saltfish is Jamaica's national dish: flaked salt cod sauteed with scotch bonnet, tomatoes and spring onion, served with tinned ackee or plantain. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Ackee arrived in Jamaica from West Africa in the eighteenth century. Paired with the salt cod that was traded as cheap food for enslaved people, it became Jamaica's defining national dish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Soak the salt cod in cold water for at least 12 hours, changing the water twice, before cooking.

glossaryTerms.definition: A tropical fruit with a rich, buttery texture; Jamaica's national fruit, eaten as a vegetable.
Soaking salt cod in fresh water over several hours to remove most of the curing salt.

content.text: the salt cod properly is the most important step in this dish. Change the soaking water at least twice over 12 hours. Under-desalted cod will make the finished dish far too salty and will mask the other flavours.

from a tin is perfectly good here and what most people use outside Jamaica. The flesh is soft and buttery with a mild flavour. It goes in last and is folded gently through the saltfish mixture rather than stirred, so it stays in pieces.

items.prepNote: substitute: use 400g tinned ackee if available

content.text: Drain the soaked salt cod and put it in the large saucepan. Cover with fresh water and bring to a boil. Simmer for 15 minutes. Drain, cool slightly, then flake into large pieces, removing any skin and bones.
Heat the vegetable oil in the large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the onion, peppers and scotch bonnet for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the tomato, spring onion and thyme. Cook for 3 more minutes until the tomato has softened.
Add the flaked saltfish and stir gently to combine. Cook for 2 minutes to heat through and let the flavours come together.
Fold in the drained tinned ackee (or cooked plantain) gently so it does not break up. Heat for 1 minute and serve with boiled dumplings, fried plantain or rice.

attrs.problem: The dish is still very salty after cooking.
attrs.solution: The cod was not soaked long enough. For very salty cod, soak for up to 24 hours and change the water three times. Taste the raw soaked cod before cooking.

attrs.problem: The ackee has broken into mush.
attrs.solution: Tinned ackee is fragile. Fold it in very gently at the end and remove the pan from the heat as soon as it is warmed through.
Use both red and green pepper and let the tomatoes cook down until they have collapsed. A pinch of paprika adds colour without changing the flavour significantly.

content.text: Ackee and saltfish is Jamaica's national dish and its most beloved breakfast. It is eaten on weekend mornings with fried dumplings, boiled green banana and fried plantain. In the UK it is served in Caribbean restaurants and home kitchens across London and Birmingham.
